passage: At the community centre in Guwahati, the counsellor Bhupen held up a card in safety class. "Some touch feels comfortable, like a hug from someone you trust. Other touch leaves you scared or muddled. Your private parts are yours. Only a grown-up helping you wash, or a doctor with Mama there, may need to touch them." Sabina, five, stared, her hands very still. "If someone says it's a secret?" "Tell a grown-up you trust, like Mama, even if they said not to." "Mama," said Sabina. Later Bhupen knelt beside her. "You can come and talk to me any time."

qa.q: Who is the counsellor at the community centre?
qa.a: The counsellor is Bhupen.

qa.q: What might Sabina have been thinking when she asked about a secret?
qa.a: She seems to be trying to understand what to do if someone asks her to keep a secret, and her stillness suggests she was thinking hard about it. She may also have felt unsure or a little worried.

qa.q: What message should the child take from the class?
qa.a: If a touch ever feels bad or someone says to keep it secret, Sabina should tell a grown-up she trusts, like Mama or Bhupen.

qa.q: How might Sabina's mother feel when Sabina tells her what she learned?
qa.a: She may feel glad that her daughter knows who to tell, and she can listen calmly and take her seriously. 🤍

grounding: A child learns that safe touch feels comfortable, unsafe touch feels scary, and secrecy is a signal to tell a trusted adult.

passage: I help at the after-school club, and I overheard Shankar, six, talking to his friend by the water cooler. "My cousin's friend touched me where he shouldn't. It felt yucky. He said it's a secret." Lokesh stood still. "Secrets like that aren't okay. That's what Ms Bindu told us. Tell a grown-up." I walked over and knelt beside them. "Thank you for telling me, Shankar. You did the right thing, and it's not your fault." I stayed with the boys and asked another helper to fetch the head teacher straight away.

qa.q: Who said that secrets like that aren't okay?
qa.a: Lokesh said that Ms Bindu told them so.

qa.q: What might Shankar have been feeling when he said it felt yucky?
qa.a: He seemed uncomfortable and confused about what happened, and worried about the secret. He may also have feared he would get in trouble.

qa.q: What should an adult do when a child tells them about unsafe touch?
qa.a: Stay with the child, listen calmly, say it is not their fault and send someone to fetch the head teacher that same day so the child is protected.

qa.q: How might Lokesh feel when he tells his friend to speak up?
qa.a: He may feel worried for Shankar and a bit unsure, but he remembers what he was taught.

grounding: A child recognises unsafe touch and secrecy, and a trusted adult responds by listening and getting help.

passage:
Monday: Vishal, Ojas's father, read him a picture book about touch. “Safe touch feels good, like a high five or a hug you want. Private parts are the ones your underwear covers. Nobody should touch them or ask you to keep touch a secret.”
Wednesday: At the clinic, the doctor asked, “Can I check your tummy?” with Papa right there. Ojas said, “Papa's here, so okay.”
Friday: Ojas told Papa, “Cousin tickled me too much and I said stop.” Papa hugged him. “Good job saying stop.” That evening he told the cousin tickling stops when someone says stop.

qa.q: What did the doctor ask Ojas on Wednesday?
qa.a: “Can I check your tummy?”

qa.q: What does Ojas's comment at the clinic show about his thinking?
qa.a: It shows he felt safe and trusted the check because Papa was there and the doctor asked first. He was using what he learned from the book.

qa.q: What did Vishal do on Friday, and why was it right?
qa.a: He praised Ojas for saying stop and spoke to the cousin that evening, showing Ojas that his no matters and adults will act.

qa.q: How might the cousin see the tickling rule?
qa.a: The cousin might have thought tickling was just fun, but learns that it stops when someone says stop.

grounding: Over a week, a child learns about safe touch and private parts, and his father acts when he reports tickling that felt too much.

passage: School was starting in ten minutes and Nitin was hunting for Disha's shoe when she said, “Papa, a big boy in the van said let's play a secret game. He tried to put his hand under my shorts. I pushed him and moved seats.” Nitin stopped. He sat on the floor beside her. “Thank you for telling me. You did exactly right. It is not your fault.” He listened to all of it. Then he rang the school principal, drove Disha himself, and stayed while the principal took notes.

qa.q: What did Disha do when the boy tried to touch her?
qa.a: She pushed him and moved seats.

qa.q: What might Disha have been feeling when she told her father?
qa.a: She was probably confused and scared by what the boy did, and worried about the secret game. Telling Papa shows she trusted him.

qa.q: What did Nitin do that a trusted adult should do?
qa.a: He stopped everything, listened calmly, said it was not her fault, and told the principal the same morning while staying with her.

qa.q: How might the principal see Nitin's report?
qa.a: The principal would take it seriously and act to keep Disha and other children safe in the van.

grounding: A child tells her father about unsafe touch and a request for secrecy, and he responds the same morning by listening and telling the school.

passage: In the city nursery, Keerthana Ma'am held up two cards: a hand giving a high five, and a stop sign. “Safe touch feels okay, like a hug from Amma when you want one. Unsafe touch feels muddled or scary inside, or someone touches where your swimsuit covers.” Hafsa's hand went up. “What about secrets?” “Surprises are fine, like a birthday present, because everyone finds out soon. But secrets about touch? Never. Tell a grown-up you trust.” Hafsa nodded seriously. “I'll tell Ammi and you.”

qa.q: What did Keerthana Ma'am hold up?
qa.a: Two cards: a hand giving a high five, and a stop sign.

qa.q: What was Hafsa thinking about when she asked about secrets?
qa.a: She was curious and a little unsure how secrets fit with the touch rules, and wanted to understand the difference.

qa.q: How did Keerthana Ma'am explain surprises versus secrets?
qa.a: She said surprises are fine because everyone finds out soon, but secrets about touch should never be kept and should be told to a trusted grown-up.

qa.q: How might Hafsa's Ammi feel hearing that Hafsa would tell her?
qa.a: She would likely feel reassured and trusted, knowing Hafsa sees her as a safe person to tell.

grounding: A teacher helps preschoolers learn safe and unsafe touch and that secrets about touch should be told to a trusted adult.

passage:
"Mummy, what's a safe touch?"

Bhavna put down the book from school. "A hug you want. A high-five. Holding hands to cross the road. It feels okay."

"And unsafe?"

"Touch that feels scary or confusing. And nobody touches the parts your swimming costume covers, except to keep you clean or healthy, with me there."

Naveen thought, scratching his ear. "What about tickling? When Bhaiya tickles and I say stop and he doesn't stop, I don't like it."

"Thank you for telling me, beta. When you say stop, it stops. I'll talk to Bhaiya this evening."

"And if someone says keep it secret?"

"Then you tell me, or Teacher, straight away."

qa.q: What examples of safe touch did Bhavna give?
qa.a: A hug you want, a high-five, and holding hands to cross the road.

qa.q: What was Naveen feeling about Bhaiya's tickling?
qa.a: He felt uncomfortable and upset when the tickling carried on after he said stop, and probably a bit confused because tickling is meant to be fun.

qa.q: What did Bhavna do well when Naveen told her about the tickling?
qa.a: She thanked him, told him clearly that "stop" should be respected, and said she would speak to Bhaiya that same evening.

qa.q: How might Bhaiya see the tickling differently from Naveen?
qa.a: Bhaiya probably thinks it is just a game, without noticing that it stops feeling fun for Naveen when he says stop.

grounding: It shows a child learning that safe touch feels comfortable, unsafe touch feels confusing, private areas are protected and secrets about touch should be told.
